name: mealpy-48b48c3c-blind20-ots
instr:
# mealpy: twenty silent breakages across the optimizer collection, diagnosed without a test suite

I drive everything here the same way: build a searcher from the settings its documentation lists, hand it an objective over a five-dimensional box with lower and upper bounds, let it run, and read the best candidate back as an array of coordinates as long as the bounds. That flow now fails in a great many places at once, while plenty of the other searchers still run end to end. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything I was able to reproduce by hand.

Setting one up is the first thing that breaks. The flocking searcher given a flight frequency of 10, a probability of 0.8, two coefficients of 1.5, two unit factors and a constant of 0.5 never returns an object, because one of the numbers I pass is treated as lying outside the permitted range. The plain crossover-and-mutation searcher does the same with a crossover probability of 0.9 and a mutation probability of 0.01: one of the two is rejected before a single round runs. The reef-style searcher given an occupancy of 0.4, a broadcast rate of 0.9, four small rates of 0.1, gammas of 0.02 and 0.2 and five trials also cannot be set up as documented, and on the occasions it is built, reading its settings back no longer reproduces what I handed it. The helper that sweeps a grid of settings is unusable in the same way: handing it a plain dictionary mapping setting names such as the round count and t
